pattern.title: Data Sufficiency
pattern.description: Is the data enough to answer?

questions.questionText:
Two drums contain water. Quantities are whole numbers of litres.
What is the quantity in the first drum?
Statement I: The quantity in the first drum and the quantity in the second drum add up to 48 litres.
Statement II: The quantity in the second drum is 31 litres.
Which of the following is correct?

options.text: Statement I alone is sufficient, but statement II alone is not sufficient
Statement II alone is sufficient, but statement I alone is not sufficient
Either statement I alone or statement II alone is sufficient
Both statements together are sufficient, but neither statement alone is sufficient

questions.explanation: Statement I is not enough: with first = 17, second = 31 the answer is 17 litres, but with first = 1, second = 47 it is 1 litres. Statement II is not enough: with first = 17, second = 31 the answer is 17 litres, but with first = 1, second = 31 it is 1 litres. Taking both together fixes the answer uniquely as 17 litres. Hence: both statements together are sufficient, but neither statement alone is sufficient.
